newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki slightly off as Nokia struggles back.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki slightly off as Nokia struggles back.

text.p: Shares ended a trendless Wednesday session off lows as Nokia met support around 300 markka and pared earlier losses, brokers said.
The HEX general index fell 0.19 percent to 2,860.51 points as advancers beat decliners 57 to 46 with 21 issues unchanged. Volume was a fair 733 million markka.
The dollar took a breather, and investors took profits from forestries and other exporters which have advanced with it recently.
Telecoms major Nokia closed down 1.00 at 305.00 markka after dipping to 297.50 markka earlier.

But paper machine maker Valmet and diversified diesel engine group Metra were stronger and active -- Valmet was up 1.70 markka at 95.70 and Metra rose 2.50 to 304.50 after announcing a strong dividend and a bonus issue.
"The market cheered Metra's report, but the group's earnings were modest," one broker said. Metra posted an 894 million markka profit compared to an 897 million median forecast.
Finland's largest banking group Merita also made a downward correction, down 0.40 at 18.30 markka.

Wholesaler and retailer Kesko fell 1.20 markka to 74.00 as brokers said they would wait for final confirmation that the EU will allow it to keep the Anttila retail chain after selling most of Tuko to restore competition on the Finnish market.
Brokers said they would eye the dollar and Nokia's moves overnight for direction.
"The market looks fragile as the dollar's upward trend came to a halt and there seems to be plenty of Nokia on sale in the U.S.," said one.
